nodes.label: Animated ASCII field [data-ascii]: two stacked pre layers draw plasma noise through a density ramp ( .:-=+*#%@) at about 24 fps with a mouse and 15 fps on touch, with the ImDev mark dissolving in and out on the bright layer and a cursor or tap ripple; sized to the card (cols×rows in the header), held still while the page scrolls, paused off-screen or in a hidden tab, one static frame under reduced motion
nodes.norm_label: animated ascii field [data-ascii]: two stacked pre layers draw plasma noise through a density ramp ( .:-=+*#%@) at about 24 fps with a mouse and 15 fps on touch, with the imdev mark dissolving in and out on the bright layer and a cursor or tap ripple; sized to the card (cols×rows in the header), held still while the page scrolls, paused off-screen or in a hidden tab, one static frame under reduced motion
nodes.rationale: Plain text in two pre elements (a dim field and a bright mark layer) instead of a canvas keeps the effect monochrome and styleable from CSS, and contain:strict on .ascii keeps each redraw from touching layout outside the card. The requestAnimationFrame loop draws every 42ms with a fine pointer and every 66ms on touch, skips frames within 140ms of a scroll event so it never competes with scrolling, and advances its clock only on drawn frames (at most 0.1s per step), so it resumes where it stopped without a jump. It runs only while an IntersectionObserver reports the field visible and the tab is not hidden; a ResizeObserver re-measures the character grid. Under reduced motion it draws a single frame (t = 2.4s) and attaches no pointer handlers. Mouse moves steer the ripple; a touch tap lights it for 1.1s.

nodes.label: Cursor-stretch kinetic type stretch(zone, letters, amp): letters near the mouse stretch vertically through --sy (CSS scale on .ht-c and .kc), batched in requestAnimationFrame; applied to the hero headline letters (amp .2) and the I build letters (.kc, grouped per word in no-wrap .kn boxes; amp .24); fine pointers and motionOK only
nodes.norm_label: cursor-stretch kinetic type stretch(zone, letters, amp): letters near the mouse stretch vertically through --sy (css scale on .ht-c and .kc), batched in requestanimationframe; applied to the hero headline letters (amp .2) and the i build letters (.kc, grouped per word in no-wrap .kn boxes; amp .24); fine pointers and motionok only
nodes.rationale: The pull falls off with horizontal and vertical distance from each letter's centre and resets on pointerleave; touch and pen pointers are ignored. Using the individual CSS scale property keeps the stretch independent of the transform-based letter reveal and of the parallax transform on the title, and a .35s scale transition smooths it.

nodes.label: drawWave(): cubic Bezier path through the timeline node centres, sets the SVG viewBox and --len for the stroke-draw animation, skipped while the wave is hidden
nodes.norm_label: drawwave(): cubic bezier path through the timeline node centres, sets the svg viewbox and --len for the stroke-draw animation, skipped while the wave is hidden
nodes.rationale: Built from the measured node positions so the curve passes through the dots at any width; --len lets the stroke draw itself when the timeline is revealed.

nodes.label: Flying portrait card (.fly): two-faced clone of img/portrait.webp (.fly-f / .fly-b with backface-visibility hidden) that travels from slot a (hero) into slot b (About), flipping once on the way; driven by a CSS scroll-driven animation (.fly.sda) where supported, by renderFly on mouse/trackpad browsers without it, while touch browsers without it keep the two static cards
nodes.norm_label: flying portrait card (.fly): two-faced clone of img/portrait.webp (.fly-f / .fly-b with backface-visibility hidden) that travels from slot a (hero) into slot b (about), flipping once on the way; driven by a css scroll-driven animation (.fly.sda) where supported, by renderfly on mouse/trackpad browsers without it, while touch browsers without it keep the two static cards
nodes.rationale: One clone sized to slot b stands in for both portrait slots (hidden via .has-fly) so the photo appears to fly. Two stacked faces, the back one pre-rotated 180deg, show the photo the right way round after the flip with no image swap or class toggle mid-scroll. The card is only built when motionOK and either scroll-driven animations or a fine pointer are available, and it stays hidden until startHero adds has-fly and the card-in intro, which Back to top replays.

nodes.label: Hero headline letter split [data-title] with hover scramble on fine pointers (motionOK only, .ready reveal with a 2.5s CSS failsafe)
nodes.norm_label: hero headline letter split [data-title] with hover scramble on fine pointers (motionok only, .ready reveal with a 2.5s css failsafe)
nodes.rationale: The visual lines are aria-hidden while the full name and role sit in an .sr span; under .js-motion the title and the portrait card stay hidden until startHero marks the hero .ready, and a 2.5s CSS failsafe keeps them from ever staying invisible.

nodes.label: Light theme palette: html[data-theme=light] token overrides

nodes.label: measureFly(): reads the small-viewport height from an svh probe element, measures slot a and slot b into geo (centres, widths, scroll end where slot b sits centred), sizes the fly card to slot b and writes --ax / --ay / --as / --bx / --by / --fend for the scroll-driven path; hides the fly card when a slot is not laid out
nodes.norm_label: measurefly(): reads the small-viewport height from an svh probe element, measures slot a and slot b into geo (centres, widths, scroll end where slot b sits centred), sizes the fly card to slot b and writes --ax / --ay / --as / --bx / --by / --fend for the scroll-driven path; hides the fly card when a slot is not laid out
nodes.rationale: A hidden 100svh probe gives the small-viewport height, so the address bar showing or hiding on phones does not move the end of the path; with scroll-driven animations the measured geometry goes into CSS variables and the compositor does the rest.

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion CSS override: 1ms animations and transitions, scroll-behavior auto
nodes.norm_label: prefers-reduced-motion css override: 1ms animations and transitions, scroll-behavior auto
nodes.rationale: One universal rule also stops the CSS-only loops that have no JS gate (hero grain, ticker marquee, timeline ping, route march). The scroll-driven classes (.fly.sda, .sda-hero) are only added by JS when motionOK, so they never run under reduced motion.

nodes.label: relayout(): recomputes hero height, measureFly + renderFly + drawWave; relayoutSoon throttles it to one run per animation frame on resize, load, fonts.ready and a ResizeObserver (hero, About, timeline); also run at startup, by startHero and on language change
nodes.norm_label: relayout(): recomputes hero height, measurefly + renderfly + drawwave; relayoutsoon throttles it to one run per animation frame on resize, load, fonts.ready and a resizeobserver (hero, about, timeline); also run at startup, by starthero and on language change
nodes.rationale: The fly geometry and the wave path depend on rendered text, so they are re-measured after load, once webfonts are ready, on resize and after a language switch; the requestAnimationFrame throttle folds bursts of resize and ResizeObserver callbacks into one measurement per frame.

nodes.label: renderFly(y): JS fallback for mouse/trackpad browsers without scroll-driven animations: cubic ease-in-out lerp of position and scale with a perspective rotateY 0-180deg along the same path; no-op when the CSS scroll-driven version runs
nodes.norm_label: renderfly(y): js fallback for mouse/trackpad browsers without scroll-driven animations: cubic ease-in-out lerp of position and scale with a perspective rotatey 0-180deg along the same path; no-op when the css scroll-driven version runs
nodes.rationale: Uses the same eased path and 0-to-end scroll range as the CSS fly-path keyframes, so mouse/trackpad browsers without scroll-driven animations see the same flight; touch browsers without them get no JS flight because a main-thread animation would trail touch scrolling.

nodes.label: renderHero(y): mouse/trackpad-only fallback for the hero headline scroll parallax (translateY -0.28 × scroll) where CSS scroll-driven animations are missing, idle past 1.3x the hero height
nodes.norm_label: renderhero(y): mouse/trackpad-only fallback for the hero headline scroll parallax (translatey -0.28 × scroll) where css scroll-driven animations are missing, idle past 1.3x the hero height
nodes.rationale: The parallax normally runs as the CSS scroll-driven hero-par animation (the same ratio, -28svh over the first 100svh); this JS path only runs on mouse/trackpad browsers without scroll-driven animations, and touch browsers without them keep a still headline.

nodes.label: renderPill(v): a gentle wobble of the nav pill's ImDev letters from scroll velocity (clamped to ±24), mouse/trackpad only
nodes.norm_label: renderpill(v): a gentle wobble of the nav pill's imdev letters from scroll velocity (clamped to ±24), mouse/trackpad only

nodes.label: renderTicker(v): with a fine pointer, eases the ticker's Web Animations playbackRate toward 1 + min(1.6, |v| × 0.06) (at most 2.6x), reversed while scrolling up, and pushes it via updatePlaybackRate only when it moves by more than 0.02; reports whether the rate is still settling
nodes.norm_label: renderticker(v): with a fine pointer, eases the ticker's web animations playbackrate toward 1 + min(1.6, |v| × 0.06) (at most 2.6x), reversed while scrolling up, and pushes it via updateplaybackrate only when it moves by more than 0.02; reports whether the rate is still settling
nodes.rationale: The animation handle comes from getAnimations() only when motionOK and the pointer is fine, so touch devices keep the plain CSS loop. Pushing only meaningful rate changes avoids re-syncing the compositor animation every frame, and returning the settling state keeps the scroll loop requesting frames after scrolling stops, until the ticker has eased back to its normal forward speed.

nodes.label: Responsive breakpoints: 1100px two-column folders and a vertical experience timeline rail; 1100px portrait (tablets) centred hero; coarse pointers get a lighter nav-pill blur; 900px single column for about, stack, kinetic band (320px ASCII card, 10px glyphs), contact, footer and case grid; 760px hero, kinetic type, form and band; 420px folders
nodes.norm_label: responsive breakpoints: 1100px two-column folders and a vertical experience timeline rail; 1100px portrait (tablets) centred hero; coarse pointers get a lighter nav-pill blur; 900px single column for about, stack, kinetic band (320px ascii card, 10px glyphs), contact, footer and case grid; 760px hero, kinetic type, form and band; 420px folders
nodes.rationale: The experience timeline becomes a vertical rail already at 1100px, before its five columns get cramped, and portrait tablets get the same centred hero as phones. On coarse pointers the nav pill swaps its 18px blur and saturate backdrop for a lighter 10px blur over a more opaque background, which is cheaper to composite while touch scrolling.

nodes.label: scrambleIn(): staggered letter reveal (--d) with a requestAnimationFrame random-glyph scramble from the GL set
nodes.norm_label: scramblein(): staggered letter reveal (--d) with a requestanimationframe random-glyph scramble from the gl set

nodes.label: Scroll-linked motion loop frame(): smoothed scroll velocity drives renderFly, renderHero, renderPill and renderTicker each animation frame, continuing while the ticker rate settles (listener only when motionOK and with a fine pointer)
nodes.norm_label: scroll-linked motion loop frame(): smoothed scroll velocity drives renderfly, renderhero, renderpill and renderticker each animation frame, continuing while the ticker rate settles (listener only when motionok and with a fine pointer)
nodes.rationale: Only mouse/trackpad browsers attach the scroll listener; where scroll-driven animations exist renderFly and renderHero return at once, so the loop mostly steers the pill wobble and the ticker rate.

nodes.label: startHero(): one-shot hero intro once document.fonts.ready resolves or after 1.2s, whichever comes first: relayout(), then has-fly and the fly card intro, marks the hero .ready and runs scrambleIn()
nodes.norm_label: starthero(): one-shot hero intro once document.fonts.ready resolves or after 1.2s, whichever comes first: relayout(), then has-fly and the fly card intro, marks the hero .ready and runs scramblein()
nodes.rationale: Waiting for the web fonts means the headline letters and the fly geometry are measured with the final font metrics, so nothing re-flows mid-intro. The 1.2s timeout caps the wait on slow font loads and the started flag makes the second trigger a no-op; until then CSS (.js-motion .hero:not(.ready)) hides the title and portrait card, with a 2.5s failsafe so they can never stay invisible. The fly card is only revealed when measureFly produced geometry.

nodes.norm_label: theme toggle [data-theme-toggle]: dark/light switch saved as imdev-theme-v2, circular view transition reveal from the button
nodes.rationale: Dark is the default and light only swaps tokens; the circular View Transition grows from the button and is skipped when motion is reduced or the browser lacks startViewTransition.

nodes.label: Kinetic word rotator (kinReset, scrambleTo): every 3.2s the I build word scrambles through ASCII glyphs into the next of six EN / ID focus areas (Business Systems, Indoor Navigation, Financial Platforms, RAG Chatbots, Real-time Games, Automations) and updates the dots and 01-06 index; pauses on hover, off-screen or in a hidden tab; also splits the I build lead into .kc letters grouped per word in no-wrap .kn boxes
nodes.norm_label: kinetic word rotator (kinreset, scrambleto): every 3.2s the i build word scrambles through ascii glyphs into the next of six en / id focus areas (business systems, indoor navigation, financial platforms, rag chatbots, real-time games, automations) and updates the dots and 01-06 index; pauses on hover, off-screen or in a hidden tab; also splits the i build lead into .kc letters grouped per word in no-wrap .kn boxes
nodes.rationale: Runs only under motionOK; otherwise the first focus area stays static. The words exist in both languages and kinReset re-renders the current one when the language flips, so the JS-written word follows the bilingual rule without paired [lang] elements. Each letter settles on its own randomised frame (34ms ticks) and glyphs are HTML-escaped before innerHTML. The .kin-word box has a fixed two-line height (1.8em) with layout and paint containment, so longer words and scramble glyphs never re-flow the band. The same block splits the I build lead into .kc letters for the cursor stretch and wraps each word's letters in a no-wrap .kn box with a plain space between words, so the lead only wraps between words; when every letter was its own inline block joined by a non-breaking space, phones broke the Indonesian Saya membangun mid-word (MEMBANG / UN). At 760px and below the lead and the rotating word also drop to clamp(34px,10.6vw,64px), so the longest word still fits a 320px screen. Pausing while the pointer is over the copy lets a reader finish the word.

nodes.norm_label: hero section #top: < full stack / developer /> headline, portrait card (slot a), imdev label and {{ ai-driven engineering }} tag over a film-grain layer
nodes.rationale: The film grain (a fractal-noise SVG on .hero::before) only breathes (opacity .08 to .15 over 7s) on fine pointers in the dark theme; touch devices and the light theme keep a static grain, so no full-viewport layer animates on phones. The headline and portrait card stay hidden under .js-motion until startHero marks the hero .ready, with a 2.5s CSS failsafe.

nodes.label: motionOK — prefers-reduced-motion gate (with the boot script's js-motion class and the CSS override): no scramble, cursor stretch, word rotation, ASCII animation, scroll-driven ticker, flying portrait, parallax, reveals, band motion or View Transition under reduced motion
nodes.norm_label: motionok — prefers-reduced-motion gate (with the boot script's js-motion class and the css override): no scramble, cursor stretch, word rotation, ascii animation, scroll-driven ticker, flying portrait, parallax, reveals, band motion or view transition under reduced motion
nodes.rationale: Project rule: keep all motion gated by prefers-reduced-motion. Scripts check motionOK before splitting, scrambling, stretching, rotating the I build word, animating the ASCII field, steering the ticker, building the flying card or adding the scroll-driven classes (.sda, .sda-hero), parallaxing, revealing or animating the band; the ASCII field then shows one static frame and the I build word stays on its first focus area. Intro states only apply under html.js-motion, so content stays visible with reduced motion or without JS; the CSS media query cuts any remaining animation, such as the ticker marquee and the hero grain, to 1ms.

nodes.label: CSS scroll-driven motion (animation-timeline: scroll(root block)): flying portrait card .fly.sda (keyframes fly-path from --ax / --ay / --as to --bx / --by over 0 to --fend of scroll) and hero headline parallax .sda-hero .hero-title (keyframes hero-par to -28svh over the first 100svh); on when motionOK and CSS.supports('animation-timeline: scroll()')
nodes.norm_label: css scroll-driven motion (animation-timeline: scroll(root block)): flying portrait card .fly.sda (keyframes fly-path from --ax / --ay / --as to --bx / --by over 0 to --fend of scroll) and hero headline parallax .sda-hero .hero-title (keyframes hero-par to -28svh over the first 100svh); on when motionok and css.supports('animation-timeline: scroll()')
nodes.rationale: Scroll-driven animations run on the browser's compositor, so the card's flight and the headline parallax stay locked to the scroll position, also on phones where JS scroll handlers lag behind native scrolling (Chrome, Edge and Safari 26+ support them). JS only measures the geometry into CSS variables (measureFly) and does no per-frame work. renderFly and renderHero remain as fallbacks for mouse/trackpad browsers without support, while touch browsers without support keep the two static portrait cards and a still headline rather than a JS animation that would trail touch scrolling. The fly path uses an ease-in-out curve (cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)) that matches the JS fallback's cubic ease.

nodes.rationale: The visible lead, rotating word, dots and ASCII card are aria-hidden; an .sr h2 (What I build / Yang saya bangun) and an .sr sentence listing all six focus areas in EN and ID carry the content for screen readers. nodes.label: graphify usage rules: graphify query/path/explain before grep or file reads, wiki/index.md for navigation, GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad review, graphify update . after code changes, graph.json diffs expected
nodes.norm_label: graphify usage rules: graphify query/path/explain before grep or file reads, wiki/index.md for navigation, graph_report.md only for broad review, graphify update . after code changes, graph.json diffs expected
nodes.rationale: query/path/explain return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output; `graphify update .` is AST-only with no API cost; graph.json is rewritten whole on every build, so a large diff in a pull request is expected and is not churn or a reason to skip the rebuild or its hooks.

nodes.rationale: graphify treats index.html as a document, not code, so the AST-only `graphify update .` never refreshes its nodes; only the skill-driven rebuild does.

nodes.label: Bilingual EN/ID system: paired [lang] elements hidden via html[data-lang] (tanyasaya-chat excluded) plus data-ph / data-al / data-alt attribute pairs
nodes.norm_label: bilingual en/id system: paired [lang] elements hidden via html[data-lang] (tanyasaya-chat excluded) plus data-ph / data-al / data-alt attribute pairs
nodes.rationale: Every visible text ships in EN and ID (project rule in CLAUDE.md). One CSS rule hides the inactive language, so switching is a single data-lang flip with no re-render; tanyasaya-chat is excluded so the chat widget, which manages its own language, is never hidden by the page rule. Text that JS writes, such as the rotating I build word, comes from EN / ID lists keyed by lang() and is re-rendered on a switch.
